raw_md:
# AMZN (Amazon.com Inc.) — Value Investor Note

## Circle of Competence
Understandable at the business-model level: Amazon sells retail goods (thin-margin, high-volume), cloud infrastructure (AWS - high-margin, capital-intensive), and advertising (high-margin, data-driven). No exotic financial engineering. The genuine stretch is forecasting near-term earnings through the current AI-infrastructure capex supercycle, where reported metrics (FCF yield of 0.11%, forward P/E above trailing P/E) say the market is digesting a real earnings air pocket rather than a steady compounding story this year.

## Moat & Durability — Score 8/10
AWS remains the dominant public cloud franchise with real switching costs - migration friction, egress fees, and deep API/tooling lock-in - and still supplies the bulk of AMZN's high-margin operating income even though the blended operating margin (13.7%) reflects retail's much thinner economics. Prime membership plus the largest logistics network in the business gives retail genuine scale and network-effect advantages, and advertising is a fast-growing, high-margin third leg riding on first-party purchase-intent data few competitors can match. The moat is real but not bulletproof: cloud/AI compute is a capital-intensity game where this year's capex, not the existing installed base, determines next year's share versus Azure and Google Cloud, and retail margins face constant pressure from low-cost cross-border entrants (Temu, Shein, TikTok Shop). That combination of durability with a live competitive-investment race is why this is an 8, not a 9-10.

## Management & Capital Allocation
A 30.6% ROE combined with 19.6% revenue growth at a $2.9T market cap shows management is still finding real reinvestment opportunities, not manufacturing returns with leverage - debt/equity near 45.6% looks like moderate, largely lease/data-center-related debt rather than balance-sheet strain. What can't be verified from this packet: AWS segment-level capex returns, the split between AI-infrastructure spend and organic growth capex, buyback cadence (Amazon pays no dividend and has historically repurchased stock only opportunistically), or Andy Jassy's capital-discipline track record on the scale Bezos-era decisions were judged. Trust here is inferred from consolidated returns, not confirmed project-level discipline.

The FCF yield of just 0.11% is the single most striking number in this packet - implied free cash flow is only around $3.2B against a $2.9T market cap, meaning essentially all operating cash flow is currently being plowed back into the business, almost certainly AI/data-center capex. That is either Amazon doing what it has always done best (out-investing competitors to widen the AWS moat before they can respond) or a real risk that this capex cycle doesn't earn adequate incremental returns before needing to be replaced or depreciated - this packet gives no way to tell which. The fact that forward P/E (26.2x) sits above trailing P/E (21.7x) - implying forward EPS roughly 17% below trailing EPS - suggests the market itself is pricing a near-term earnings dip before any capex payoff shows up in the numbers.

## Predictability
Revenue growth of 19.6% and a 30.6% ROE support the 'easy to understand' business-model case, but the earnings picture is murkier: the multiples imply forward EPS roughly 17% below trailing EPS, and current FCF per share is close to zero. That is a real, packet-visible earnings air pocket, not noise, and it fails Munger's 'easy decision' test on near-term owner earnings even though the long-run demand story for cloud, e-commerce, and advertising is not seriously in doubt. Momentum data reinforce a market that has already re-rated the stock higher on the growth story (+29.5% 6m, +21.1% 12m, RSI14 68.6) ahead of that earnings dip resolving either way.

## Inversion — How an Owner Loses Money From Here
1. **AI capex outruns AI returns**: AWS/data-center spend keeps consuming nearly all free cash flow (0.11% yield today) without a commensurate acceleration in AWS growth or margin, leaving the company depreciation-heavy and capital returns compressed for years - the bear case for every capital-intensive infrastructure race.
2. **Retail margin erosion**: low-cost cross-border competitors (Temu, Shein, TikTok Shop) keep undercutting price on commoditized goods, capping the already-thin blended operating margin (13.7%) even as top-line growth continues.
3. **Multiple de-rating from a stretched entry point**: at an implied ~26x forward earnings, RSI14 near 69, and the stock already up 29% over six months, any growth, margin, or regulatory disappointment (AWS deceleration, antitrust action) invites a swift re-rating lower, amplified by the stock's elevated beta (1.45).

## Valuation
The packet does not give share price or count directly. Backing into per-share terms using an approximate ~10.5B diluted share count (a modeling assumption, not sourced from the packet) implies a current price near $278/share, trailing EPS near $12.78, and forward EPS near $10.61 - consistent with the forward-P/E-above-trailing-P/E signal that near-term earnings are expected to dip. Current FCF/share is negligible (~$0.31) given the capex supercycle, so a straight FCF-multiple valuation is not meaningful this year; instead this uses a normalized-owner-earnings approach that looks through the capex spike.

Normalized owner earnings, haircut from trailing EPS for stock-based comp and capex-cycle noise, are estimated near $10.90/share.
- **Low case** (conservative: capex cycle proves less productive than hoped, growth decelerates toward high-single-digits, 11% discount rate reflecting the elevated beta): ~17x normalized owner earnings → ~$185/share.
- **High case** (AI capex monetizes well through AWS reacceleration and advertising, growth resumes toward low-double-digits, 9% discount rate): ~25x normalized owner earnings → ~$270/share.

Midpoint ~$228/share vs. an implied current price of ~$278/share gives a margin of safety of roughly **-22%** - the market is paying up today for a payoff (AI-driven AWS reacceleration) that hasn't shown up in the earnings yet. This is a real, high-quality business priced for a good outcome, not a business priced with room for one.

## The Cloning Caveat
David Tepper's Appaloosa Management added a genuinely large position (7.51% of portfolio, share count nearly doubled, +98.2%) - a real, high-conviction statement from a concentrated macro/equity manager, not an index-hugging allocation. Seth Klarman's Baupost Group holds 4.06% of portfolio; Klarman is a famously price-disciplined deep-value investor, so his willingness to own AMZN at all is a meaningful data point even if 4% isn't a max-conviction bet for his fund. ShawSpring (5.3%), Ackman/Pershing Square (2.8%), and Egerton Capital (2.79%) round out several substantial, non-trivial positions, alongside new stakes from Sound Shore (2.64%) and Leon Cooperman (1.16%). This is broad, credible accumulation by quality-oriented managers - real corroboration that this is a business worth owning - but it is not proof that today's price offers a margin of safety, and several of the largest holders here (Tepper, Ackman) run concentrated macro/event books rather than classic deep-value ones, which changes what their buying signals about price discipline specifically.

## Verdict
**Watch, conviction 6/10.** Amazon clears the circle-of-competence, durable-moat, and (inferred) trustworthy-management bars comfortably. It fails the sensible-price test: the packet's multiples imply a price near $278/share against an estimated normalized-owner-earnings fair value of roughly $185-270/share, a negative margin of safety of about 22%. The near-zero current FCF yield and forward-EPS-below-trailing-EPS signal both point to a real, ongoing capex supercycle whose payoff is not yet visible in the numbers - a legitimate 'great business, not-yet-great price' situation. Superinvestor buying (Tepper, Klarman, Ackman, ShawSpring, Egerton and others) corroborates business quality, not valuation discipline; this is a name to own on a real pullback, not to chase at the current implied price.
momentum_thesis:
AMZN's trend is intact and reaccelerating, not extended: the stock chopped
sideways for three months (ret_3m +0.80%) before the tape turned in the last
month (+8.27%), and the 6- and 12-month returns (+29.47%, +21.08%) confirm the
underlying uptrend never broke — price sits 12.9% above its 200DMA with RSI14
at 68.6, warm but short of textbook overbought. Positioning offers no squeeze
tailwind: short interest is negligible (1.0% of float, 2.1 days to cover), so
this isn't short-covering fuel, it's a market with essentially no bearish bet
to unwind — upside has to come from fresh buying and downside has no
short-covering cushion either. Options skew leans constructive (put/call OI
0.54, more calls open than puts), consistent with dealers positioned for
continued upside rather than hedging a top. The superinvestor tape is the
strongest input here: sixteen managers added or initiated in Q1/Q2 2026,
several at real conviction size — Tepper +98% shares to 7.5% of book, Hong
+57% to 5.3%, Klarman +47% to 4.1%, Ackman +19% to 2.8% — spanning macro,
value, and activist styles, which reads as broad-based smart-money
confirmation of the technical trend rather than late-cycle chasing. Net: this
is a resumption pattern with fundamental sponsorship behind it, not a blow-off.
